children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

First, could you please tell me how many children you would like to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names and ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi! Thanks for helping me with this. I'd like to claim for my son Alex, he's 16 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! It's great to meet you, and I'm happy to help assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Since Alex is 16 years old, I need to ask a few more questions to determine your eligibility.

Is Alex currently in approved education or training? This would include things like:
- A-levels or equivalent
- Scottish Highers
- NVQs up to level 3
- Home education (if started before they turned 16 or after 16 if they have a statement of special educational needs)
- Traineeships in England

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex isn't in any education or training at the moment. He finished his GCSEs and decided not to continue with sixth form or college.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know. Since Alex is 16 and not currently in approved education or training, there are a couple of other circumstances that could still make you eligible for Child Benefit for him.

Has Alex registered with either:
- A government-sponsored careers service, or
- The armed services?

If so, you may be able to continue receiving Child Benefit for up to 20 weeks after leaving education.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he hasn't registered with a careers service or the armed forces. He's just been taking some time to figure out what he wants to do next.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that.

I have one more question to check another possible scenario: Has Alex started any paid work of 24 hours or more per week, or is he receiving any benefits in his own right (such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not working at all right now, and he's not receiving any benefits in his own name either.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information.

I also need to confirm a couple more things about your own circumstances:

1. Do you live in the UK?
2. Does Alex live with you?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - we're in Manchester. And yes, Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that.

Based on the information you've provided, I now have enough details to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Let me summarise the situation:
- Alex is 16 years old
- He is not in approved education or training
- He has not registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services
- He is not working 24+ hours per week
- He is not receiving benefits in his own name
- You live in the UK (Manchester)
- Alex lives with you

Unfortunately, based on the rules for Child Benefit, I need to deliver some disappointing news.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on my assessment, I'm sorry to say that **you are not currently eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

**Reason:**
For children aged 16 or over, Child Benefit eligibility normally continues only if the child remains in approved education or training. There is an alternative provision where Child Benefit can continue for up to 20 weeks if a 16 or 17 year old leaves education and registers with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services. Since Alex has finished his GCSEs, is not in approved education or training, and has not registered with either of these services, you do not currently meet the eligibility criteria.

**What you could do:**
- If Alex decides to return to approved education or training (such as A-levels, a college course, or an NVQ up to level 3), you may become eligible again.
- If Alex registers with a government-sponsored careers service, you could potentially claim Child Benefit for up to 20 weeks.

I hope this helps clarify your situation. If Alex's circumstances change, please do consider re-assessing your eligibility. Is there anything else I can help you with?
